title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving

output_modality.value: future semantic segmentation maps (single view, 2D), predicted autoregressively over up to three steps

control_signal.value: ego action: speed and yaw rate, past actions plus the mean future action; derived from vehicle odometry (Cityscapes) or GPS (BDD100K)

control_mechanism.value: FiLM: an MLP encodes the action vector and scales and shifts every U-Net block; compared with input-level concatenation of constant action planes and with no action input

base_model.value: U-Net with four levels (64 to 512 channels), GroupNorm, GELU, residual copy-last term; trained from scratch, 12.55 M to 13.07 M parameters; SegFormer-B5 supplies segmentations

datasets.value: Cityscapes (2,975 train, 500 val snippets), BDD100K tracking clips (1,528 clips kept), plus a synthetic environment with action-dependent dynamics

metrics.value: mIoU and MO-mIoU (movable objects) under true action and under interventions (shuffled, zero yaw, stop, mean); also parameters, GFLOPs, latency

controllability_evidence.value: Test-time action interventions: executed action adds at most 2.46 mid-term mIoU on Cityscapes, while shuffled action lowers FiLM by 23.17; synthetic: FiLM 87.95 vs 59.99 no action, shuffled -31.57

closed_loop.value: No; open-loop autoregressive forecasting only, mid-term horizon 0.54 s (Cityscapes) and 0.6 s (BDD100K), no driving policy in the loop

stated_limitations.value: Interventions measure strength of action dependence, not its correctness; forecasts and metrics are class level, not per agent; larger video or occupancy models and longer horizons left as future work

notes: Not a generative video or sensor world model; a small semantic forecaster used as a probe of how strongly forecasts depend on the ego action. Page labels for limitations are approximate.
